scope: Warrior 전투도끼 낙하 도끼 급강하와 접촉 폭발 전면 재제작

sourcePolicy.primaryRevisionGoal: 유성이나 추상 압력체가 아니라 큰 외날 전투도끼 머리가 짧고 빠르게 내려와 박히고, 접촉점에서 물리적인 폭발이 터지는 연출로 다시 만든다.
sourcePolicy.preservedTimingBoundary: 웹 타격 시점은 875ms를 유지한다. 첫 접촉 F13, 최대 폭발 F15, 폭발 유지 종료 F16이다.
sourcePolicy.userImpactLanguage: 도끼가 팍 내려찍히고 즉시 폭발하는 한 번의 강한 타격

commonPrompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production 2D combat VFX overlay sprite sheet for AlarmQuest. Create exactly 16 chronological frames in a strict 4-column by 4-row, row-major sprite sheet. Every cell is one independent wide 361:160 combat viewport; final sheet 1444:640; Detailed hand-painted high-resolution 2D rendering; transparent RGBA; clean antialiased alpha; image-rendering auto; no pixel art. Motion grammar: AXE_SNAP_SLAM_CONTACT_EXPLOSION. Keep the camera, crop, perspective, axe-head design, blade angle, contact point, and explosion origin mathematically fixed across all cells. The visual subject is one clearly readable massive single-bladed bearded battle-axe head made of dark chipped gunmetal, with a short section of thick dark wooden or wrapped shaft entering from the upper-right and cropped by the top edge. No character holds it. The axe head must have a straight reinforced poll, one broad curved cutting edge, a visible eye around the shaft, and an asymmetric silhouette that cannot be mistaken for a comet, fireball, crescent projectile, hammer, sword, or abstract energy blob. Fix one downward-left attack line at 18 degrees from vertical and one immutable blade-bite point P=(51%,78%). F01 is almost transparent. F02-F06 show only restrained weight pressure and one faint metal glint in the upper-right; do not reveal the whole axe or move it through the screen. F07-F09 keep the axe mostly above the crop with compressed air gathering at the same upper-right entry, creating anticipation without a slow visible fall. The actual drop is a sharp three-frame snap: F10 axe head enters at center=(63%,14%), F11 crosses center=(58%,41%), F12 reaches center=(53%,68%) just above P. These three samples must advance monotonically downward with increasing distance per frame, identical silhouette, identical 18-degree angle, no rotation, no sideways recoil, no scaling, and no redraw wobble. Place exactly three to five thin, tapered, translucent blue-gray descent streaks behind the shaft and axe head in F10-F12, parallel to the fixed attack line and anchored to one upper-right vanishing origin; the streaks make the drop feel instantaneous but never form a background panel. F13 is the first physical contact: the lower quarter of the cutting edge bites into P with one compact ivory-orange flash and a short V-shaped metal-pressure notch; no full explosion before this frame. F14 is the compression frame: the axe head stops dead and remains embedded at exactly the same angle while a low asymmetric pressure wedge, two short cracks, and a few chunky gunmetal and ochre fragments push outward from P. F15 is the unique maximum: a forceful ground-rooted contact explosion erupts from P around the visibly embedded axe head, with a hot ivory-white core, restrained orange-ochre flame tongues, one low wide broken pressure fan, six to ten chunky steel and stone fragments, and two short upward air tears. The explosion must spread wider than it is tall, touch neither full top edge nor all four edges, preserve transparent corridors, and read as physical impact rather than magic. Keep the axe head partly readable through and above the blast so the cause of the explosion remains obvious. F16 holds the same embedded axe and the same explosion at 75-85% of F15 energy: slightly opened fragments and shorter flame tongues, but no fade to empty, no rebound, no weapon recovery, and no second blast. Playback ends on this impact tableau at 1,000ms. Palette: dark gunmetal axe, cold blue-gray wind pressure, ivory-white impact core, restrained amber and burnt ochre explosion accents. Treat every cell as separately clipped with no adjacent-frame residue. Render the weapon and attached VFX only: no warrior body, hands, enemy, scenery, painted sky, ground plane, UI, text, labels, numbers, grid, borders, gutters, padding, or opaque background.

skills.name: 전투도끼 낙하
skills.generationPrompt: Regenerate '전투도끼 낙하' from scratch so the viewer instantly reads one massive battle axe snapping downward and exploding on impact. The previous comet-like and abstract pressure versions are diagnosis only and must not be imitated. Design one broad single-bladed bearded gunmetal axe head with a reinforced back, visible shaft eye, chipped curved cutting edge, and a short heavy shaft cropped at the upper-right frame edge. Preserve that exact weapon drawing, scale, and 18-degree downward-left angle in every visible frame. Keep F02-F09 as restrained offscreen weight anticipation; do not slowly float the weapon down. Make the real motion occur only in F10, F11, and F12, moving the same axe head through the declared centers in one accelerating snap, with three to five straight attached descent streaks behind it. F13 must feel like a hard 'PAK': the blade abruptly bites the fixed lower-middle point and all long wind streaks terminate there. F14 compresses the stopped axe and contact wedge. F15 detonates one compact but forceful low-wide physical explosion around the still-visible embedded axe head: white-hot contact core, amber-ochre flame pressure, broken steel fan, six to ten chunky fragments, and short air tears, all rooted at P. Avoid a neat circle; use a heavy asymmetrical wedge that expands mostly sideways along the contact surface. F16 holds this same impact at 75-85% energy and ends while the explosion is still readable. Lock the brightest core in F13-F16 within x=49%-53%, y=75%-81%, and keep the axe blade bite inside that same box. The result must communicate one instant axe slam and one explosive impact without camera shake, a magical blast, or a second finisher.
